findings.message: Task 1.4's e2e criteria AC1, AC3, and AC4 (backend per-model readiness gating, fail-verdict rendering, simulated-connection-failure handling) have no recorded red proof — unlike AC2, which was validated with one. Their tests have never been observed failing, so per the ledger's own legend they are not yet evidence of anything beyond 'ran once and passed'.
findings.why_not_fixed: Producing a red proof requires mutating the pipeline/route-handling code and re-running the real GPU-backed Playwright project (real Whisper/Qwen/TTS models loaded, ~30s+ per run) — hardware and model weights not available in this review context. The task's own gate:human manual-verification section already substitutes substantial human-observed evidence (5/5 e2e cases passed against the real backend, AC3's fail verdict rendered visibly distinct from AC2's pass) for part of this risk, but that is not equivalent to a recorded mutation-based red proof.

options.option: Accept the manual-verification note as sufficient compensating evidence for a gate:human task and leave AC1/AC3/AC4 without formal red proofs permanently
options.consequence: Matches how this task was actually executed and gated, but leaves these three criteria's tests unvalidated against a known-failing mutation — a future regression in readiness-polling or connection-failure handling could pass silently if the e2e suite itself has a latent bug.

options.option: Require a follow-up task/session with real GPU hardware to run mutation-based red proofs for AC1, AC3, AC4 and record them under red-proofs/
options.consequence: Closes the gap properly but costs another full GPU-backed e2e run cycle (cold model load + ~30s per mutation × 3 criteria) for a phase that is otherwise complete and already human-gated.

findings.recommendation: Accept the manual-verification note as sufficient compensating evidence for a gate:human task and leave AC1/AC3/AC4 without formal red proofs permanently
